newsitem.title: CHINA: China opens Chenglingji port to foreign vessels.
newsitem.headline: China opens Chenglingji port to foreign vessels.

text.p: China has opened Chenglingji river port in Yueyang city, in the central province of Hunan, to foreign vessels from Monday, the Xinhua news agency said in an overnight report.
Chenglingji is the 16th port along the Yangtze river to open to foreign vessels, Xinhua said, quoting the State Port Administration Office.
The opening of the port was part of China's efforts to speed development of the Yangtze river region and promote economic growth of China's central and western regions, officials said.
Previously, foreign vessels could sail as far as Wuhan, capital of the central province of Hubei, along the Yangtze -- or less than 1,100 kilometres (684 miles) from the coast.
Chenglingji is about 1,300 km (808 miles) from the coast.
Since 1991, China has spent 100 million yuan ($12 million) to renovate Chenglingji port, Xinhua said. It now has annual cargo handling capacity of 600,000 tonnes.
